rationale: CompositeMoneyColumn extends BiCompositeColumn with transformFromValue (MonetaryAmount -> BigDecimal number + CurrencyUnit pair) and transformToValue (rebuilds a MonetaryAmount through Monetary.getDefaultAmountFactory(), returning null if either part is null), plus the nullable() extension. Ruled out CompositeMoneyColumnType.kt (only the Table.compositeMoney registration overloads), CurrencyColumnType.kt (maps one CurrencyUnit to a 3-char varchar, no amount handling) and core CompositeColumn.kt (generic BiCompositeColumn base that just invokes the lambdas supplied here).

query: When the library writes generated schema-change SQL into a script on disk, how does it wipe whatever the file held before and add a terminating semicolon only to statements lacking one?
rationale: MigrationUtilityApi.writeMigrationScriptTo creates the File, truncates it with writeText(""), skips blank statements and appends each statement followed by ';' only when it does not already end in one, plus a newline. Ruled out the jdbc and r2dbc MigrationUtils.kt (generateMigrationScript only collects statements and calls this inherited helper) and exposed-plugin-core MigrationGenerator.kt (writes its own files with an unconditional joinToString(";\n", postfix = ";"), no truncate-then-append or conditional semicolon).

query: What check rejects a batched save of many records rendered as one SQL text once the number of bound placeholders passes the engine's ceiling, and which embedded engine has a lower ceiling?
rationale: MultiRowValuesInsertStatement.validateLastBatch multiplies data.size by the table's column count and throws BatchDataInconsistentException above 65535 bind parameters, or 32766 when currentDialect is SQLiteDialect. Ruled out BatchInsertStatement.kt (its validateLastBatch only checks column defaults and required columns, no parameter count), SQLServerBatchInsertStatement.kt (caps the batch at 1000 rows, not parameters) and the jdbc/r2dbc executables (just dispatch to this statement).

query: How does a dropdown menu in the top bar open when the mouse hovers over its button, yet avoid immediately closing again when the click that follows the hover arrives?
rationale: VPFlyout.vue keeps an open flag and an openedByHover flag: onPointerEnter opens the panel for mouse pointers, onPointerLeave closes it unless the pointer moved into the button or panel, and toggle() swallows the click that follows a hover-open instead of closing the menu; it also handles Escape and outside pointerdown. Ruled out composables/flyout.ts (only tracks focusin and calls onBlur, no hover logic), VPMenu.vue (renders the item list inside the panel) and VPNavMenuGroup.vue / VPNavBarExtra.vue (merely embed VPFlyout).

query: How does the default theme postpone loading the hosted lookup widget's heavy script until the user clicks or presses a keyboard shortcut, while opening a network connection to the provider early during idle time?
rationale: VPNavBarSearch.vue only mounts the async Algolia box after loadAndOpen() flips loaded (triggered by the button click or the Ctrl/Cmd+K, Ctrl/Cmd+I and / key handlers), and its onMounted hook injects a preconnect link to the provider host inside requestIdleCallback. Ruled out VPAlgoliaSearchBox.vue (the widget itself, already loaded by then), VPLocalSearchBox.vue (the built-in index UI) and VPNavBarSearchButton.vue (a plain button), and support/docsearch.ts (option and mode resolution only).

query: How does the build determine every page's last-edit date in one pass over the revision history instead of spawning a separate process for each page?
rationale: cacheAllGitTimestamps runs a single streamed git log --name-only over the markdown files and feeds it through the GitLogParser Transform to fill a path-to-timestamp Map, while getGitTimestamp reads that cache and only falls back to a per-file git log -1 on a miss. Ruled out plugin.ts (just calls cacheAllGitTimestamps when lastUpdated is enabled), markdownToVue.ts (calls getGitTimestamp to set pageData.lastUpdated) and VPDocFooterLastUpdated.vue (only renders the date).

query: How are the translated versions of a page cross-referenced as alternates in the crawler-facing XML file, and how is each entry's last-modified date filled in?
rationale: generateSitemap groups pages by their locale-independent path (stripping the locale directory), then emits each variant with a links array of all variants and a lastmod taken from pageMetaMap, applies sitemap.transformItems and streams sitemap.xml into outDir. Ruled out build.ts (only invokes generateSitemap), plugin.ts (defines PageMeta/lastUpdated data) and VPNavTranslations.vue (adds client-side hreflang alternate head links, not the XML file).

query: How does the client warm up the JavaScript for pages linked from the current screen once those anchors scroll into view, but hold back on poor connections or data-saver mode?
rationale: usePrefetch observes the #app anchors with an IntersectionObserver, skips them while useNetwork reports offline, saveData or a 2g effectiveType (isWeak), and for visible routable links injects a link rel=prefetch (viaDOM) or an XHR (viaXHR) for the page chunk path, remembering fetched chunks in hasFetched. Ruled out router.ts (supplies getRoutableLinkUrl and navigation, no prefetch scheduling), utils.ts (pathToFile only maps a URL to a chunk path) and index.ts (merely calls usePrefetch).

query: Which rules say a table row may hold only cell elements and that a hyperlink cannot sit inside another hyperlink, since browsers would otherwise silently restructure the markup?
rationale: html-tree-validation.js holds the disallowed_children and autoclosing_children tables plus is_tag_valid_with_parent and is_tag_valid_with_ancestor (tr only allows th/td, a forbids a descendant a). Ruled out: the compiler visitors RegularElement/Text/ExpressionTag and the parser's element state, which only call these functions to emit errors or warnings and define no rules themselves.

query: Which module makes a value glide toward a newly assigned target with a bouncy, physically simulated motion, and clamps long frame gaps so a backgrounded tab does not make it jump wildly?
rationale: motion/spring.js contains tick_spring (stiffness, damping, inverse mass, precision settle check), the deprecated spring() store and the Spring class, and both loops clamp elapsed time to 1/30th of a second. Ruled out: motion/tweened.js, which animates over a fixed duration with an easing function and has no stiffness or damping physics, and motion/index.js which only re-exports and adds a reduced-motion media query.

query: How can a custom class's getter start listening to an outside data source only while some effect is reading it, and stop once the last reader is gone?
rationale: reactivity/create-subscriber.js exports createSubscriber, which counts active render effects, calls the user's start callback once when the count goes from zero to one, and runs the returned teardown when the last effect is destroyed (after a microtask). Ruled out: reactivity/media-query.js and reactivity/window/* which are only consumers of it, and store/shared/index.js whose writable() has a similar start/stop but for stores, not effect-tracked getters.

query: When a click lands on a button inside a mounted app, which routine walks up through the ancestors calling their registered handlers, and how does it stop an outer mounted app from running them a second time?
rationale: internal/client/dom/elements/events.js defines handle_event_propagation, which walks event.composedPath(), looks up per-element handlers stored under event_symbol, and uses the marker set on the event object to skip nodes already handled by an inner mounted app. Ruled out: internal/client/render.js which only attaches the root listeners calling it, the public events/index.js which re-exports on(), and compiler Attribute visitors which only decide whether a handler is delegable.

query: How does the compiler keep the extra specificity from component style isolation down to a single class-worth, however many compound selectors one rule chains together?
rationale: compiler/phases/3-transform/css/index.js render_stylesheet and its ComplexSelector/SelectorList visitors append the scoping class to the first scoped selector and use a :where() wrapper afterwards via state.specificity.bumped, so only one class of specificity is added. Ruled out: phases/2-analyze/css/css-analyze.js and css-prune.js, which only compute metadata such as scoped/used and never edit the output text, and phases/css.js which holds small helpers.

query: How are nested plain objects and arrays inside component state made reactive per field on first access, while class instances and values that are already wrapped are left untouched?
rationale: internal/client/proxy.js exports proxy(), which only wraps values whose prototype is Object.prototype or Array.prototype and that lack STATE_SYMBOL, and whose get/set/has/deleteProperty traps lazily create one source per property plus a version source and a length source for arrays. Ruled out: internal/client/reactivity/sources.js which supplies the signal primitives but no wrapping logic, and the svelte/reactivity collection classes such as map.js and set.js which are separate reactive containers.

query: When one assignment changes several stores that a computed store depends on, how does the computed one wait until all of them hold their new values before recalculating?
rationale: store/shared/index.js: writable().set calls each subscriber's invalidate callback before running queued subscribers via subscriber_queue, and derived() tracks a pending bitmask per input store so sync() only runs once pending is zero. Ruled out: store/index-client.js and store/index-server.js which only re-export these and add toStore, store/utils.js (subscribe_to_store wrapper) and internal/client/reactivity/store.js which handles the auto-subscription of dollar-prefixed stores in components.

query: During server-side output generation, how does the framework decide which of several nested components' document title declarations ends up in the page head?
rationale: internal/server/renderer.js: Renderer.title() records each title with its tree path from get_path(), and SSRState.set_title does a depth-first lexicographic path comparison so only a later or deeper path replaces the stored value; #close_render appends get_title() to the head. Ruled out: compiler/phases/3-transform/server/visitors/TitleElement.js which only emits the $$renderer.title call, and the client-side TitleElement visitor, which assigns document.title in the browser.

query: When a route declares output definitions for several status codes, how does the framework choose the one that applies to a given response, considering exact codes, class wildcards, a catch-all and media-type variants?
rationale: lib/schemas.js getSchemaSerializer(context, statusCode, contentType) looks up the compiled response serializer in the route context: the exact status code first, then the '<digit>xx' class wildcard, then 'default'; when the entry is a per-media-type map it uses the reply media type, then '*/*', else returns false. Ruled out: lib/validation.js compileSchemasForSerialization only compiles and stores the per-status map; lib/reply.js serialize() and lib/error-handler.js fallbackErrorHandler merely call getSchemaSerializer.

query: When a route declares expected headers using mixed-case names, how does the framework make the check still work against the lowercase header names Node provides?
rationale: lib/validation.js compileSchemasForValidation copies a plain-object headers definition and lower-cases both its 'required' entries and its 'properties' keys (skipped for custom validators or non-plain schema objects) before handing it to the compiler. Ruled out: lib/schema-controller.js (selects and builds the validator compiler, never touches header names), lib/route.js (only calls compileSchemasForValidation), lib/request.js (only exposes validateInput, no name normalisation).

query: How does the framework stop reading a body that grows beyond the configured size limit, both when the announced length is already too large and when chunks keep arriving?
rationale: lib/content-type-parser.js rawBody() rejects up front when the content-length header exceeds the limit, then counts received bytes in the 'data' listener (onData) and aborts with FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE once the running total or encoded length passes the limit, detaching its listeners. Ruled out: lib/route.js validateBodyLimitOption (only checks the option is a positive integer), lib/handle-request.js (decides whether to run the body reader but never reads or counts bytes), lib/request.js routeOptions (just reports the limit).

query: How does the framework answer a call whose URL matches no registered route, and how can a sub-scope with its own URL prefix install a separate fallback for unmatched paths below that prefix?
rationale: lib/four-oh-four.js builds a dedicated find-my-way router for unmatched URLs: basic404 sends the default 404 JSON body, setNotFoundHandler registers a prefix-scoped catch-all (prefix + '/*') with its own Context, hooks and error handler, and refuses a second handler on the same scope. Ruled out: fastify.js (setNotFoundHandler there is a thin wrapper delegating to this module), lib/plugin-override.js (only calls arrange404 for prefixed scopes), lib/reply.js (a small guard against recursion inside a 404 handler).

query: When a sub-module is registered, how does the framework give it an isolated scope that inherits everything from its parent yet keeps its own additions from leaking back?
rationale: lib/plugin-override.js override(old, fn, opts) creates the child instance with Object.create(old), registers it in the parent's children list, and gives it its own copies of the reply and request constructors, content-type parser set, hooks, schema controller, route prefix, log serializers and registered-plugin chain, unless the function opts out of encapsulation. Ruled out: lib/plugin-utils.js (registration bookkeeping, naming, dependency and version checks), fastify.js (only assigns avvio.override), and the helpers it calls such as lib/hooks.js buildHooks, which each copy a single concern.

query: When a callback that runs before the incoming payload is consumed returns a replacement stream, how does the framework swap it in so that later stages read the new stream?
rationale: lib/hooks.js preParsingHookRunner iterates the pre-parsing callbacks, passing the current payload stream and, when a callback calls next(err, newPayload) or its promise resolves with a stream, stores it into request[kRequestPayloadStream] so the next callback and the body reader use it. Ruled out: lib/route.js runPreParsing (only seeds the stream with the raw request and invokes the runner), lib/content-type-parser.js (just reads whatever stream is stored).

query: How does the framework work out the real client IP address, host name and scheme when it sits behind a reverse proxy, and how does it decide which hops to trust?
rationale: lib/request.js buildRequestWithTrustProxy defines ip, ips, host and protocol getters on the request prototype using getTrustProxyFn (boolean, hop count, comma-separated list or function compiled via proxy-addr) and reads x-forwarded-host and x-forwarded-proto only when the socket peer is trusted. Ruled out: fastify.js (only passes options.trustProxy into buildRequest) and lib/config-validator.js (generated option schema).

query: When a developer-supplied failure callback itself throws while processing a failure, how does the framework retry with an outer scope's callback and finally fall back to a plain built-in response?
rationale: lib/error-handler.js handleError runs the route's callback and, before calling it, stores Object.getPrototypeOf(errorHandler) (the parent scope's entry built by buildErrorHandler) in reply[kReplyNextErrorHandler]; if that one throws, the next attempt uses the parent, and when the chain is exhausted fallbackErrorHandler serialises a minimal JSON body directly on the raw response. Ruled out: lib/reply.js (runs onError hooks then calls handleError), lib/route.js and lib/four-oh-four.js (only build the chain with buildErrorHandler), lib/error-serializer.js (generated serializer).

query: How does the library turn nested timestamps, enumerations, decimal numbers and unique identifiers in a returned structure into plain values that can be written out as JSON?
rationale: jsonable_encoder in fastapi/encoders.py recursively converts models, dataclasses, dicts, lists, Enums, dates/times (isoformat), Decimal (decimal_encoder) and UUID (str) via the ENCODERS_BY_TYPE table. Ruled out fastapi/routing.py (serialize_response only calls it as a fallback) and fastapi/openapi/docs.py (merely imports it).

query: How is a single pushed message with multi-line text, an optional comment and a reconnect delay laid out as bytes for a browser that is subscribed to a continuous event feed?
rationale: format_sse_event in fastapi/sse.py builds the wire bytes: ': ' comment lines, 'event:', one 'data:' line per line of text, 'id:', 'retry:', and the terminating blank line. Ruled out fastapi/routing.py, whose _serialize_sse_item only chooses the data string and then calls format_sse_event, and which owns the keep-alive logic that this question does not ask about.

query: How does the framework make sure that tearing down a synchronous resource-managing dependency cannot deadlock when every worker thread in the shared pool is already busy?
rationale: contextmanager_in_threadpool in fastapi/concurrency.py runs cm.__enter__ in the shared pool but runs cm.__exit__ with a fresh CapacityLimiter(1) so cleanup never waits for a free thread. Ruled out fastapi/dependencies/utils.py, whose _solve_generator merely calls this helper to wrap sync generator dependencies.

query: How does the interactive API explorer page keep user-supplied configuration values from breaking out of the inline script block when they are embedded as JSON?
rationale: _html_safe_json in fastapi/openapi/docs.py json.dumps the value and escapes <, > and & as \u003c, \u003e, \u0026; get_swagger_ui_html uses it for the parameters and for init_oauth inside the <script> tag. Ruled out fastapi/applications.py (only registers the page routes and calls get_swagger_ui_html) and fastapi/encoders.py (converts values to JSON-compatible types but does no HTML escaping).

query: How do the form-based login dependencies turn a single space-separated permissions string into a list, and which variant insists the grant type be a fixed literal value?
rationale: OAuth2PasswordRequestForm.__init__ in fastapi/security/oauth2.py does self.scopes = scope.split(), and OAuth2PasswordRequestFormStrict redeclares grant_type as required with Form(pattern='^password$'). Ruled out the sibling fastapi/security/http.py, api_key.py and open_id_connect_url.py (header/credential schemes with no form fields) and the SecurityScopes class in the same file, which is a different scope concept (scopes declared by dependencies).

query: When a path operation declares exactly one payload argument versus several, how does the framework decide whether the JSON body maps directly to it or must be nested under each argument's name?
rationale: _should_embed_body_fields in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py returns True when there is more than one distinct body field name, when the first field is explicitly embedded, or when a single Form/File field is not a BaseModel; request_body_to_args then uses that flag. Ruled out fastapi/routing.py (APIRoute.__init__ just calls the function and stores the result) and fastapi/params.py (defines the Body 'embed' attribute only).

query: When a request arrives with no content type header, or with a structured-syntax suffix like +json, how does the framework decide whether to decode the body as JSON or leave it as raw bytes?
rationale: The inner app() inside get_request_handler in fastapi/routing.py reads request.headers['content-type']; with no header it parses JSON only if strict content type checking is off, otherwise it parses JSON only for application/json or application/*+json and falls back to body_bytes. Ruled out fastapi/dependencies/utils.py (request_body_to_args receives the already-chosen bytes/JSON body) and fastapi/applications.py (only forwards the strict flag).

query: In what order are the internal error-catching layers and user-registered wrappers nested around the request dispatcher, and why is the layer that closes uploaded files placed innermost?
rationale: FastAPI.build_middleware_stack in fastapi/applications.py builds the list ServerErrorMiddleware, then user_middleware, then ExceptionMiddleware, then AsyncExitStackMiddleware, and wraps self.router with it in reverse; its comment explains the contextvars reasoning for the innermost placement. Ruled out fastapi/middleware/asyncexitstack.py, which only implements the file-closing layer itself and does not decide where it sits.

query: How does a single verb call turn a temporary column selection into group keys and row locations, and why does it refuse when the input table already carries persistent groups?
rationale: R/by.R: compute_by() resolves the per-call grouping selection (eval_select_by, compute_by_groups using vec_group_loc to build keys and the .rows list) and check_by() aborts when the input is already a grouped_df or rowwise_df. Ruled out: R/group-by.R (persistent group_by, only calls compute_by with a NULL selection) and R/mutate.R, R/summarise.R, R/filter.R, R/slice.R, R/reframe.R, which merely call compute_by.

query: How can I merge a table of changes into another one so matching identifier values are overwritten and unseen identifiers are appended, while duplicated identifiers in the changes table are rejected?
rationale: R/rows.R: rows_upsert.data.frame() matches key columns with vec_match, overwrites the matching values with vec_assign, appends the unmatched y records through rows_bind, and rows_check_unique() rejects duplicate keys in y. Ruled out: R/join.R and R/join-rows.R (they compute matches for joins but never modify a table from keyed changes), R/coalesce.R and R/bind-rows.R (no keyed matching).

query: How is a shorthand for two intervals overlapping expanded into elementary comparison operators, and how do exclusive endpoints change which operators are used?
rationale: R/join-by.R: parse_join_by_overlaps() (with binding_join_by_overlaps and check_bounds) expands overlaps(x_lower, x_upper, y_lower, y_upper, bounds=) into a pair of <=/>= conditions for closed bounds and a pair of </> conditions for any open bound. Ruled out: R/join-rows.R (consumes the already parsed conditions to locate matches), R/join-cols.R (output column naming) and R/join.R (verbs and docs, no overlap parsing).

query: How can a function with no sorting parameter of its own, like a cumulative total, be rewritten through a wrapper so it runs on values arranged according to a separate vector and returns results in the original positions?
rationale: R/order-by.R: order_by() captures the call, rewrites it into a with_order() call, and with_order() sorts x with vec_order_radix, runs the function, then restores the original positions with the inverse permutation. Ruled out: R/lead-lag.R (shift() just calls with_order for its own order_by argument), R/nth-value.R (does its own reordering inside nth), R/arrange.R (sorts the table rows rather than a single computation).

query: What happens if an expression saved from inside a verb call tries to look up a column only after that call has already returned?
rationale: R/data-mask.R: the DataMask R6 class method forget() removes the column bindings and rebinds each one to a lazy promise that aborts with an 'Obsolete data mask ... Too late to resolve' error once the verb is finished. Ruled out: R/mutate.R, R/summarise.R, R/filter.R, R/slice.R (they only register mask$forget() with on.exit) and src/mask.cpp (binding add/remove and evaluation in C++, no late-resolution error).

query: If the default label for a new frequency column is already taken by an existing variable, how is an alternative label generated and what notice is displayed?
rationale: R/count-tally.R: check_n_name() picks the name for the new frequency column, calling n_name() which prepends 'n' repeatedly until the name is unused, and informs 'Storing counts in ..., as n already present in input'. Ruled out: R/summarise.R and R/mutate.R (generic verbs that receive the chosen name), R/utils.R and R/compat-name-repair.R (general name repair, not the frequency column).

query: How does the package compute the new left-to-right arrangement of columns when a chosen set is moved next to an anchor column, and what happens if both a before and an after anchor are given?
rationale: R/relocate.R: eval_relocate() evaluates the tidyselect selection, resolves the before/after anchors to a single position (errors when both are supplied), and builds the integer vector arranging the remaining columns on each side of the moved block. Ruled out: R/mutate.R (mutate_relocate only forwards .before/.after to relocate), R/select.R and R/rename.R (choose or rename columns without anchoring).

query: How can I label runs of adjacent equal values, or equal combinations across several vectors, with an integer that goes up each time the value changes?
rationale: R/consecutive-id.R: consecutive_id() bundles its unnamed inputs into a data frame and calls vctrs vec_identify_runs() to return an integer that increments at every change from the previous position. Ruled out: R/group-by.R and R/group-data.R (group structure by distinct value, not by runs), R/rank.R (ranking, not run labelling), R/n-distinct.R (counts distinct values only).

query: Which router resends a request to another worker when the first one has not answered within a short interval, until some reply arrives or an overall deadline expires?
rationale: TailChoppingRoutees.send shuffles the routees, schedules sending the same message to the next routee every interval, completes a promise with the first ask reply and fails with AskTimeoutException once the within duration passes. Ruled out ScatterGatherFirstCompleted.scala, which sends to all routees at once instead of staggering, and the other routing logics (Random, RoundRobin, SmallestMailbox), which pick a single routee with no retry.

query: When a network partition leaves two groups with exactly the same number of members, how does the majority-keeping policy pick which group survives?
rationale: KeepMajority.majorityDecision in DowningStrategy.scala handles thisSide == otherSide by keeping the side that holds the member with the lowest address (first in the ordered members), otherwise the larger side wins. Ruled out SplitBrainResolver.scala (the actor that gathers reachability and calls decide, with no majority or tie logic), SplitBrainResolverProvider.scala (only constructs the strategy from settings) and SplitBrainResolverSettings.scala (config parsing).

query: How does the streaming splitter decide where each top-level record ends when input arrives in arbitrary byte chunks and curly brackets can also appear inside quoted text with escape characters?
rationale: JsonObjectParser (offer/poll/seekObject/proceed) buffers ByteString chunks, tracks nesting depth on curly braces, and ignores braces inside double-quoted strings by tracking inStringExpression and inBackslashEscape; an object is emitted when depth returns to 0. Ruled out scaladsl/JsonFraming.scala, which is only a thin GraphStage wrapper that calls the parser's offer/poll, and scaladsl/Framing.scala, which does delimiter and length-field framing rather than brace matching.

query: How does the system notice that two different writers appended events for the same entity identity when its history is read back from storage, and what options exist for dealing with the stale ones?
rationale: The ReplayFilter actor compares writerUuid and sequenceNr of each ReplayedMessage, keeps a window buffer and a set of old writers, and in Fail, Warn or RepairByDiscardOld mode either throws, logs, or discards events from the overlapping older writer. Ruled out AsyncWriteJournal.scala (only maps the config string to the mode and spawns the filter), Eventsourced.scala and the typed EventSourcedBehaviorImpl/ExternalInteractions (they only stamp a writerUuid on written events).

query: What stops untrusted incoming payloads from instantiating dangerous classes when decoding JSON or CBOR, by refusing known exploit types and anything not covered by the configured bindings?
rationale: JacksonSerializer.scala defines GadgetClassDenyList (isAllowedClassName/isAllowedClass for Jackson's no-deserialization list, c3p0 DataSource and Spring application-context classes) and the checkAllowedClassName/checkAllowedClass/isInAllowList checks that require a class to be bound to a Jackson serializer or match an allowed prefix, throwing IllegalArgumentException otherwise. Ruled out JacksonObjectMapperProvider.scala (mapper feature and module configuration, no class vetting), JsonSerializable.scala (marker trait only) and JacksonMigration.scala (schema version upgrades).

query: When several lookup mechanisms for finding the network addresses of a named peer are configured in a chain, what happens if the first yields no addresses or fails with an error?
rationale: AggregateServiceDiscovery.resolve walks the configured discovery-methods list: if a method returns an empty Resolved.addresses it logs and tries the next, and recoverWith on NonFatal errors also moves on to the next method; the last method's result is returned as is. Ruled out Discovery.scala (extension that loads a method by name from config), ServiceDiscovery.scala (the abstract API and Lookup/Resolved types) and the single-method implementations dns/DnsServiceDiscovery.scala and config/ConfigServiceDiscovery.scala.

query: How does the inter-node transport make sure internal lifecycle signals to a peer arrive in order, resending periodically until acknowledged and quarantining the peer when too many pile up?
rationale: The SystemMessageDelivery GraphStage assigns increasing sequence numbers inside SystemMessageEnvelope, keeps an unacknowledged queue, resends on ResendTick, clears on Ack/Nack, throws GaveUpSystemMessageException after the give-up timeout, and on buffer overflow quarantines the association and sends to dead letters; the receiving SystemMessageAcker in the same file enforces ordering and replies Ack/Nack. Ruled out Handshake.scala (UID exchange), Control.scala (control message subject plumbing) and Association.scala (assembles the streams but holds no resend logic).

query: How does the executor that gives each worker thread its own private limited-size queue choose which queue a submitted task goes to, and what happens when that queue is full?
rationale: AffinityPool.execute picks workQueues(queueSelector.getQueue(command, parallelism)); the FairDistributionHashCache QueueSelector hashes the runnable (with a fair-work-distribution cache) so the same actor mailbox lands on the same worker queue, and a full queue or shutting-down pool goes to the RejectionHandler, whose ThrowOnOverflowRejectionHandler throws RejectedExecutionException. Ruled out PinnedDispatcher.scala (one dedicated thread per actor, no queue selection), ThreadPoolBuilder.scala and ForkJoinExecutorConfigurator.scala (JDK executor configuration) and the Aeron TaskRunner.scala (single-thread task loop).

query: For a child module declared with a bare semicolon instead of an inline body, which candidate locations on disk are tried, and how does a custom path attribute change the lookup relative to the parent?
rationale: ModDir::resolve_declaration in mod_resolution.rs builds the candidate files (name.rs then name/mod.rs, or the join_attr result when a path attribute is present), tracks directory ownership via root_non_dir_owner and enforces a depth limit. Ruled out: nameres/collector.rs only calls this to descend into modules, and ide-diagnostics unresolved_module only prints the candidates that this function returns in its Err.

query: How does the declarative macro engine keep several possible cursors alive in a rule's left-hand side while stepping through the call-site tokens, and what does it do when more than one could still be valid at the end of the input?
rationale: expander/matcher.rs implements the NFA-style simulation in match_loop and match_loop_inner, with cur_items, next_items, eof_items and bb_items thread lists, and at EOF requires exactly one eof item else reports an unexpected-token error with error recovery bindings. Ruled out: expander.rs only picks the rule and calls this, transcriber.rs substitutes bindings into the right-hand side, parser.rs parses the macro definition into ops.

query: Which rules decide that a trait cannot be used behind a trait-object pointer, such as a method without a receiver, one that mentions the implementing type in its parameters or return value, or one carrying its own type parameters?
rationale: hir-ty dyn_compatibility.rs defines DynCompatibilityViolation and MethodViolationCode and implements virtual_call_violations_for_method (static method, async fn, Self in inputs or output, generic method, undispatchable receiver), the Sized-self and supertrait checks. Ruled out: ide/src/hover/render.rs only formats the violation text for hover and hir/src/lib.rs only re-exports and wraps the query, and the tests file is not eligible.

query: When a developer types a dot after some value, how does the editor offer shortcut templates that wrap the receiver into a conditional, a match, or a loop depending on whether its type is a boolean, an optional-or-fallible enum, or an iterable?
rationale: complete_postfix in completions/postfix.rs builds the snippet items such as if, while, for, match, let, ifl, lete, branching on TryEnum (Option/Result), receiver_ty.is_bool() and IntoIterator impls. Ruled out: completions/dot.rs offers field and method completions after a dot, not these templates, and completions/postfix/format_like.rs only handles string-literal formatting snippets, which this question does not ask about.

query: Which refactoring pushes a logical negation through a chain of conjunction and disjunction operands, swapping the connective and inverting each operand, and does the equivalent trick for iterator calls that test whether any or all items satisfy a predicate?
rationale: apply_demorgan.rs holds the two assists: apply_demorgan rewrites a negated or non-negated && / || expression by swapping the operator and inverting each operand through the invert_boolean_expression helper, and apply_demorgan_iterator turns !iter.any(p) into iter.all(!p) and back. Ruled out: invert_if.rs and flip_binexpr.rs swap branches or operand order but do not distribute negation, and utils.rs only supplies the generic single-expression inversion helper that this assist calls.

query: How does the project loader find the Rust standard library source tree for a toolchain, checking an environment variable override first and falling back to installing a missing component through the toolchain manager?
rationale: project-model sysroot.rs contains discover_rust_lib_src_dir (honours RUST_SRC_PATH when it contains core, else get_rust_lib_src under lib/rustlib/src/rust/library) and discover_rust_lib_src_dir_or_add_component, which runs rustup component add rust-src when the source is missing. Ruled out: workspace.rs merely calls Sysroot::discover, and toolchain_info/* queries rustc for cfg, target and version rather than locating the library sources.

query: How does the language server turn the structured JSON error reports printed by the external cargo build into editor diagnostics, deciding which suggested replacements become preferred quick fixes and which labelled spans become related information?
rationale: diagnostics/flycheck_to_proto.rs has map_rust_diagnostic_to_lsp and map_rust_child_diagnostic, which split primary and secondary spans, build lsp Diagnostic objects, turn suggested_replacement plus applicability (MachineApplicable is preferred, MaybeIncorrect still emitted) into QUICKFIX code actions and related information. Ruled out: flycheck.rs spawns cargo and parses the message stream, and diagnostics.rs (DiagnosticCollection) only stores the already mapped results.

query: After the recursive-descent parser has produced a flat list of start, finish and token records, which routine builds the nested tree output, and how does it reorder start markers that point forward to an enclosing parent so the outer node opens first?
rationale: parser/src/event.rs defines the Event enum and the process function, which walks the flat Vec<Event>, follows forward_parent chains collecting node kinds and then enters them in reverse so the outer node opens first, also handling the float-split hack and tombstones. Ruled out: parser.rs only creates the links through Marker and CompletedMarker::precede, output.rs just stores enter/leave/token steps, and shortcuts.rs interleaves trivia afterwards.

query: When a compact daylight-saving rule text leaves out the shifted offset or the clock hour at which the changeover happens, which default values does the library fill in?
rationale: ParsePosixSpec and its helpers ParseOffset/ParseDateTime in time_zone_posix.cc break a POSIX TZ string such as PST8PDT,M3.2.0,M11.1.0 into pieces and set the defaults: the DST offset is the standard offset plus one hour and the changeover clock time is 02:00:00. Ruled out: time_zone_posix.h only declares the PosixTimeZone struct and says 'standard-defined defaults' without giving them; time_zone_info.cc merely calls ParsePosixSpec to extend transitions.

query: How does the library compute the minimum number of single-character edits between two short strings, counting a swap of neighbouring characters as one edit and giving up early past a limit?
rationale: CappedDamerauLevenshteinDistance in damerau_levenshtein_distance.cc fills a banded dynamic-programming table with deletion, insertion, substitution and adjacent-transposition costs and returns cutoff+1 when the strings differ by more than the cutoff or exceed 100 characters. Ruled out: the matching .h only declares the function; flags/parse.cc is a caller that uses it for misspelling hints but does not compute the edit count.

query: How does the library store a fixed group of heterogeneous values so that members whose types carry no data add no memory overhead?
rationale: CompressedTuple in compressed_tuple.h performs the empty base optimisation: internal_compressed_tuple::Storage keeps each element as a base class when ShouldUseBase (empty, non-final class) holds and as a data member otherwise, so a tuple of only empty types is itself empty. Ruled out: raw_hash_set.h and btree.h/inlined_vector.h merely use CompressedTuple; no other non-test source implements this storage trick.

query: How does the library cheaply detect that adding a new ordering dependency between two nodes would create a loop, by numbering nodes consistently with a topological order?
rationale: GraphCycles::InsertEdge in graphcycles.cc implements the Pearce-Kelly dynamic topological sort: it keeps a rank per node, keeps the ranks unchanged when rank[x] <= rank[y], otherwise runs ForwardDFS/BackwardDFS over the affected range, returns false if a cycle is found, and Reorder()s ranks. Ruled out: mutex.cc only calls InsertEdge on its deadlock graph to report lock-order inversions; graphcycles.h just declares the class.

query: If a second thread hits a fatal fault while another thread is still writing out the crash diagnostics, what does the library do about it?
rationale: AbslFailureSignalHandler in failure_signal_handler.cc uses the atomic failed_tid compare-exchange to detect re-entry: it logs that a signal was raised while already in the handler, and a thread other than the first sleeps 3 seconds (PortableSleepForSeconds) and then calls RaiseToDefaultHandler. Ruled out: failure_signal_handler.h only documents options and says nothing on concurrent faults; debugging/internal/examine_stack.cc formats the trace text but has no re-entry logic.

query: How does the library convert a numeric operating-system error value, such as one for a missing file or a full disk, into one of its canonical failure categories?
rationale: ErrnoToStatusCode in status.cc is a large switch over errno values such as ENOENT, ENOSPC, EACCES and EAGAIN that returns the matching absl::StatusCode (NotFound, ResourceExhausted, PermissionDenied, Unavailable, default Unknown). Ruled out: status.h only declares ErrnoToStatusCode; status/internal/status_internal.cc has MapToLocalCode, which maps raw integer status codes, not errno values.

query: How does the library fill a buffer of random 32-bit words from the operating system, and what does it fall back to when the preferred system call is unsupported by the kernel?
rationale: ReadSeedMaterialFromOSEntropy in seed_material.cc dispatches per platform: BCryptGenRandom on Windows, zx_cprng_draw on Fuchsia, and on POSIX getentropy in chunks of at most 256 bytes with a fallback to reading /dev/urandom (ReadSeedMaterialFromDevURandom) when the kernel lacks getentropy. Ruled out: seed_material.h only declares it; entropy_pool.cc only calls ReadSeedMaterialFromOSEntropy to seed its pool and reads no OS entropy itself.

query: In what order are the arguments applied when a program loads extra arguments from several named files, one of which pulls in yet another file?
rationale: In parse.cc, HandleGeneratorFlags/ReadFlagfiles push one ArgsList per --flagfile file in reverse file order onto the input_args stack, and ParseAbseilFlagsOnlyImpl always processes the most recent (top) list first, so earlier files run before later ones and a nested flagfile is expanded before the rest of its parent. Ruled out: flags/internal/flag.cc and commandlineflag code only set individual flag values and know nothing about argument-list ordering.

query: How does the library decide to leave out a class member when producing or consuming output, based on release-version markers, access-modifier flags, compiler-generated status, or an opt-in marker annotation?
rationale: Excluder.excludeField (and excludeClass) holds the decision logic: it tests the configured modifier mask, @Since/@Until against the configured version, field.isSynthetic(), the requireExpose/@Expose check and then user ExclusionStrategy lists. Ruled out: GsonBuilder (only configures the Excluder through withVersion/withModifiers/excludeFieldsWithoutExposeAnnotation), ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory (merely calls excluder.excludeField), and FieldAttributes (a read-only view of a field handed to strategies).

query: Which built-in conventions convert a camel-cased Java property identifier into forms like upper-case with underscores, lower-case with dashes, or dot-separated lower-case for the produced JSON keys?
rationale: The FieldNamingPolicy enum defines IDENTITY, UPPER_CAMEL_CASE, UPPER_CAMEL_CASE_WITH_SPACES, UPPER_CASE_WITH_UNDERSCORES, LOWER_CASE_WITH_UNDERSCORES, LOWER_CASE_WITH_DASHES and LOWER_CASE_WITH_DOTS, implemented through its separateCamelCase and upperCaseFirstLetter helpers. Ruled out: FieldNamingStrategy (only the one-method interface), GsonBuilder.setFieldNamingPolicy (just stores the choice), SerializedName annotation (explicit per-field override, no conversion rules), and the protobuf adapters which use Guava CaseFormat for a different purpose.

query: Which built-in options decide what Java class an untyped JSON numeric literal becomes, for example a long when it fits and otherwise a double, or an arbitrary-precision decimal?
rationale: The ToNumberPolicy enum implements the four strategies: DOUBLE, LAZILY_PARSED_NUMBER, LONG_OR_DOUBLE (tries Long.parseLong then falls back to a Double, rejecting NaN/infinity unless lenient) and BIG_DECIMAL. Ruled out: ToNumberStrategy (just the one-method interface), NumberTypeAdapter and ObjectTypeAdapter (only call whichever strategy is configured), and GsonBuilder setters (just store the strategy).

query: When a textual timestamp fails to match the configured pattern while parsing, which alternative formats are tried, in what order, before an error citing the offending text is raised?
rationale: DefaultDateTypeAdapter.deserializeToDate loops over its dateFormats list (US-locale format, then default-locale format, then the pre-Java-9 style format), and finally falls back to ISO8601Utils.parse before throwing JsonSyntaxException 'Failed parsing ... as Date'. Ruled out: ISO8601Utils (implements only the single ISO-8601 grammar and has no fallback chain or error wrapping), GsonBuilder.setDateFormat (just creates the adapter factory), and the java.sql/java.time adapters which handle other classes.

query: How is the maximum depth of simultaneously open brackets enforced while pulling tokens from the input, what is the default ceiling, and what error is raised when it is exceeded?
rationale: JsonReader declares DEFAULT_NESTING_LIMIT = 255, exposes setNestingLimit/getNestingLimit and enforces it in push(), which throws MalformedJsonException 'Nesting limit ... reached' when stackSize - 1 >= nestingLimit. Ruled out: JsonParser and JsonStreamParser (only catch StackOverflowError as a backstop and rethrow it as a parse exception, they do not enforce a depth limit), JsonWriter (has no nesting limit) and JsonTreeReader (walks an in-memory tree).

query: In what order does the library try strategies for creating a fresh instance of a target class while deserializing, from user-registered creators to default implementations for interface types to bypassing initialization entirely?
rationale: ConstructorConstructor.get(TypeToken, boolean) encodes the order: exact-type and raw-type InstanceCreator, special collection constructors (EnumSet etc.), the no-args constructor honouring ReflectionAccessFilter, default implementations for Collection/Map interfaces (ArrayList, LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, ArrayDeque, LinkedTreeMap/LinkedHashMap, ...), the instantiability check, and finally the Unsafe allocator. Ruled out: UnsafeAllocator (only the last-resort allocation primitive), InstanceCreator (the user hook interface), and MapTypeAdapterFactory/ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory (merely call get()).

query: How can a class hierarchy be round-tripped through JSON by embedding a discriminator property that names the concrete subclass, with every permitted subclass registered explicitly?
rationale: RuntimeTypeAdapterFactory (extras module) registers subclasses with labels via registerSubtype, writes a label property (default 'type') first in the JSON object in write(), and in read() removes/reads that property and dispatches to the delegate registered for the label, throwing JsonParseException for unregistered subclasses. Ruled out: the other extras classes (InterceptorFactory, PostConstructAdapterFactory, UtcDateTypeAdapter) which do post-processing and UTC dates, and the core JsonAdapter annotation / TypeAdapterRuntimeTypeWrapper which only pick an adapter for the runtime class without any discriminator.

query: How are protobuf messages converted to and from JSON so that enum values can appear either as integers or as symbolic labels, with per-member names overridable through schema options?
rationale: ProtoTypeAdapter (proto module) is a JsonSerializer/JsonDeserializer for Message; its EnumSerialization NUMBER/NAME setting drives getEnumValue and findValueByNameAndExtension, and getCustSerializedName / getCustSerializedEnumValue consult registered proto field and enum-value option extensions (or json_name) to override names. Ruled out: LegacyProtoTypeAdapterFactory in the same package, which is a migration aid reproducing the old reflection-derived mapping of generated class fields and offers no enum number-vs-name choice or schema-option overrides.

query: How does the library work out which line of the application's own source triggered a database call, skipping stack frames that belong to its internals and to test or generated files?
rationale: CallerFrame/callerFrame and FileWithLineNum in utils/utils.go walk runtime.Callers frames and return the first frame whose file is outside the library's source directory, is not a _test.go file and is not a .gen.go file. logger/logger.go, logger/slog.go and callbacks.go only call these helpers to prefix messages, they do not implement the frame walk, so they are ruled out.

query: How are bound parameter values substituted back into the query text for human-readable display, doubling quote characters and showing unprintable byte slices as a placeholder?
rationale: ExplainSQL in logger/sql.go converts each argument (bool, time, Valuer, Stringer, []byte, numbers, strings) to a literal, doubles the escaper character, prints non-printable byte slices as a binary placeholder, and then replaces either '?' or $n markers in the text. logger/logger.go only prints the already-rendered text, and the root callbacks.go and gorm.go just delegate to Dialector.Explain, so they are ruled out.

query: How does the library make rows that were logically removed via a timestamp column invisible to ordinary reads, and turn a remove request into a timestamp update instead of physically dropping the row?
rationale: soft_delete.go defines the DeletedAt type whose QueryClauses, UpdateClauses and DeleteClauses return SoftDeleteQueryClause, SoftDeleteUpdateClause and SoftDeleteDeleteClause; their ModifyStatement methods add the 'column is zero value' filter to reads and rewrite a removal into SET column = now. callbacks/delete.go, callbacks/query.go and schema/schema.go only iterate over or register the clauses a schema exposes and contain no timestamp logic, so they are ruled out.

query: In what order does the automatic table-sync routine process the user's models so that tables referenced by foreign keys are created first, and how does it avoid looping forever on circular references?
rationale: Migrator.ReorderModels in migrator/migrator.go parses each model's relationships into a dependency list (parseDependence), then insertIntoOrderedList emits dependencies before dependents and uses orderedModelNamesMap to avoid loops with cyclic references; AutoMigrate and CreateTable call it. The root-level migrator.go only declares the Migrator interface and migrator/column_type.go, index.go and table_type.go only describe column, index and table metadata, so they are ruled out.

query: How does the library keep automatically generated labels for foreign keys, indices and unique constraints within the database's character limit by truncating them and appending a short digest?
rationale: NamingStrategy.formatName in schema/naming.go joins prefix, table and column with underscores, and when the rune count exceeds IdentifierMaxLength (default 64) cuts the string and appends the first 8 hex characters of its SHA-1 hash; IndexName, UniqueName, CheckerName and RelationshipFKName all go through it. schema/index.go, schema/constraint.go and schema/relationship.go only call the namer to obtain names and do no truncation, and gorm.go merely sets the default length, so they are ruled out.

query: When several filter conditions are combined with AND and OR, how does the query builder decide which fragments get wrapped in brackets, and why does it move a leading single alternative condition behind another one?
rationale: clause/where.go implements Where.Build, which swaps the first expression if it is a lone OrConditions so the SQL does not start with OR, and buildExprs, which wraps an expression in parentheses when its SQL text contains ' AND ' or ' OR ' and several expressions are combined (also AndConditions.Build and OrConditions.Build). clause/expression.go only defines Expr/NamedExpr/IN/Eq builders and statement.go's BuildCondition merely constructs the expressions passed in, so they are ruled out.

query: How does the library fetch child records for a whole list of parent rows with a single extra query on the collected key values, then hand each parent only its own children?
rationale: The preload function in callbacks/preload.go collects the parents' identity values with schema.GetIdentityFieldValuesMap, runs one Find with an IN condition on the related table (via the join table for many-to-many), then loops over the results and assigns each element to the parents matching its foreign key through identityMap; preloadEntryPoint handles nested paths. callbacks/query.go's Preload is only a thin wrapper that calls preloadEntryPoint, chainable_api.go only records the requested paths, and callbacks/associations.go handles saving rather than reading, so they are ruled out.

query: When several registered handlers each ask to run before or after another named handler, how does the library compute the final execution order and report contradictory requests?
rationale: sortCallbacks in the root callbacks.go places handlers with before/after constraints (including the '*' wildcard) into a sorted name list, recursively sorts the referenced handler, returns errors such as 'conflicting callback X with before Y' and drops handlers marked removed. callbacks/callbacks.go only registers the default handlers by name in a fixed sequence, and callbacks/interfaces.go only declares model hook interfaces, so they are ruled out.

query: How does the matcher for hardware network interface addresses support an alternative separator character, and why would a value mixing capital and small hex letters be rejected?
rationale: The mac() function in v4/core/regexes.ts escapes the optional delimiter (default colon) and builds an alternation of an all-uppercase and an all-lowercase hex-pair form, so mixed case fails. Ruled out v4/core/schemas.ts ($ZodMAC only forwards def.delimiter into regexes.mac) and the classic/mini factory wrappers, which hold no matching logic.

query: When importing a standards-based description document in which a named definition points back to itself, how does the converter avoid recursing forever while building runtime validators?
rationale: In classic/from-json-schema.ts, convertBaseSchema handles a $ref by recording it in ctx.processing while it is being converted; meeting the same ref again returns a z.lazy that looks up ctx.refs later (resolveRef finds the target in $defs/definitions). Ruled out core/to-json-schema.ts and core/json-schema-processors.ts (the opposite direction, validator to document) and core/json-schema.ts (type declarations only).

query: When a validator is converted into a standards-based description, which conditions cause a nested validator to be replaced by a pointer into a shared definitions section instead of being written inline?
rationale: extractDefs in core/to-json-schema.ts walks the seen map and calls extractToDef (replacing the body with a $ref via makeURI) for the root, schemas in the external registry, schemas carrying an id in metadata, schemas on a cycle, and schemas seen more than once only when ctx.reused is 'ref'. Ruled out core/json-schema-generator.ts (legacy class that just delegates to extractDefs) and core/json-schema-processors.ts (per-type keyword emitters and the top-level entry that calls extractDefs).

query: How are the individual problems found during checking organized into a nested structure that mirrors the input, with separate branches for object members and array positions?
rationale: treeifyError in v4/core/errors.ts recursively flattens union/key/element issues and walks each issue path, creating 'properties' entries for string path segments and 'items' entries for numeric ones, with an 'errors' list at each node. Ruled out classic/errors.ts (ZodError wrapper whose format()/flatten() merely delegate) and v3/ZodError.ts (its format() nests _errors without a properties/items split).

query: When an annotation store is consulted for a validator that was cloned from another annotated one, how are the parent's annotations combined with the child's, and which identifying key is deliberately not passed down?
rationale: $ZodRegistry.get in v4/core/registries.ts follows schema._zod.parent, spreads the parent's metadata (recursively), deletes its 'id', then overlays the child's own entry, returning undefined if the merged object is empty. Ruled out classic/schemas.ts (.meta()/.describe() only write entries) and core/to-json-schema.ts (reads the registry; its flattenRef merges output keywords, not metadata lookups).

query: Which tiny helper collects lines of generated source text with consistent indentation and finally compiles them into an executable function, optionally replaying each snippet for synchronous and asynchronous modes?
rationale: The Doc class in v4/core/doc.ts: write() dedents each snippet to its minimum indent and re-indents by the current level, a function argument is invoked twice (execution 'sync' then 'async'), and compile() builds a new Function from the argument names and joined lines. Ruled out core/schemas.ts, whose $ZodObject fast path is only a consumer of Doc, and util.ts allowsEval, which only detects whether eval-style code is permitted.

query: In the older major version, how are the per-member outcomes of an object-shaped validator folded into one result, so that any hard failure voids everything, softer failures are remembered, and prototype-polluting keys or missing values are left out?
rationale: ParseStatus.mergeObjectSync in v3/helpers/parseUtil.ts returns INVALID if any key or value is aborted, calls status.dirty() for dirty ones, and skips the '__proto__' key and undefined values unless alwaysSet; mergeObjectAsync awaits then delegates to it. Ruled out v3/types.ts (ZodObject._parse only builds the key/value pairs and calls this merger) and the v4 object parser in core/schemas.ts, which has no dirty/valid tri-state.

query: Why does extending an object-shaped validator that already carries custom checks sometimes throw, and what condition decides whether adding new fields is permitted?
rationale: extend() in v4/core/util.ts throws only when def.checks is non-empty AND an incoming key already exists in the current shape (suggesting safeExtend, which has no guard); non-overlapping new keys are allowed. Ruled out classic/schemas.ts and mini/schemas.ts, whose extend methods merely call util.extend, and the sibling pick/omit/partial/merge in the same file, which throw unconditionally on checks.
